title: The PM Peak That Sent 199 Cars In, Not 306
featured_title: THE PM PEAK THAT SENT 199 CARS IN NOT 306
subject: civil

presentation.challenge: The project generated 306 total trips in the PM peak hour, but only 65% were entering. The inbound design demand was about 199 veh/h.

practice.primary_question: How are daily trip generation, peak-hour percentage, and directional split combined to estimate peak directional traffic demand?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Treating all peak-hour generated trips as if they traveled in the design direction.

case_dna.target_misconception: The total PM peak-hour trip generation is the same as inbound PM peak-hour demand.
case_dna.why_plausible: The peak-hour factor is applied correctly, but directional distribution is a separate planning step that can be overlooked.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: 400 dwelling units×8.5 trips/unit/day×9%=306 PM peak-hour trips total. Applying the 65% entering split gives 198.9 entering trips/h.
case_dna.corrected_model: Generate total trips first, apply the peak-hour fraction, then apply the directional split for the movement being designed.

problem_statement: A proposed residential development has 400 dwelling units. The planning rate is 8.5 vehicle trips per dwelling unit per day. Assume 9% of daily trips occur during the PM peak hour and the PM peak directional split is 65% entering and 35% exiting. Determine total PM peak-hour trips and entering PM peak-hour demand.
fixed_constraints: PM peak hour=9% of daily trips

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: Total peak trips were mistaken for inbound peak demand.
gates.prompt: What step follows the peak-hour conversion?

options.label: Daily trips → peak-hour trips → directional trips
options.reason: The directional split applies to the peak-hour total.

options.label: Treat all PM peak trips as entering
options.reason: The stated split says only 65% are entering.

options.label: Use daily trips as the hourly entering flow
options.reason: Daily trips must first be reduced to the peak-hour share.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Build the trip-generation chain
gates.result: The entering PM peak demand is about 199 veh/h.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove directional demand
gates.success: Daily trips=3400, PM peak total=306, entering=198.9≈199 veh/h.
gates.hint: Do not stop after the 306 total peak-hour trips.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Trip generation and directional distribution answer different questions

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the planning note
report: C2. PM peak total is 306 trips/hour.
C3. Therefore inbound PM peak demand is 306 veh/h.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: The daily trip generation is correct.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: The total PM peak-hour trips are correct.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It ignores the stated 65/35 directional split.

correction.template: PM peak total={peak_total} veh/h; entering demand≈{entering} veh/h.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Keep inbound demand at or below 180 veh/h
gates.constraint: Keep the same trip rate, peak-hour fraction, and directional split.

options.label: Limit the development to about 362 dwelling units

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply trip generation again
gates.prompt: A 250-unit project generates 9 trips/unit/day; 10% occur in the PM peak and 60% are entering. What is entering demand?

options.label: 225 veh/h
options.reason: That is total PM peak-hour traffic before directional split.

gates.explanation: Apply trip rate, time-of-day share, and directional split in sequence.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the transportation-planning calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that total peak-hour trips must be directionally distributed before sizing an inbound or outbound movement.

items.label: What failed
items.value: All peak-hour trips were assigned to one direction.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Daily trips × peak-hour fraction × directional fraction.

seo.seo_title: Trip Generation and Peak-Hour Directional Demand | FE Civil E-106
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Civil E-106: 400 homes at 8.5 trips/day, 9% PM peak, and 65% entering produce about 199 inbound veh/h, not 306.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Civil trip generation peak hour directional split
seo.excerpt: Total peak-hour trips are not automatically the directional demand used to design an access movement.
seo.direct_answer: 400×8.5=3400 trips/day. The PM peak total is 3400×0.09=306 veh/h. Applying 65% entering gives 198.9≈199 inbound veh/h.

faqs.q: How do you estimate peak directional project traffic?
faqs.a: Multiply daily trip generation by the peak-hour fraction and then by the directional split.
